title: Phetchaburi 2-Day Itinerary 2026 — Old Town, Khao Wang & Cha-Am | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 2-day, 1-night Phetchaburi itinerary in Thailand: old-town temples, cafes and famous sweets, the climb up Khao Wang, then a night in Cha-Am with fresh beachside seafood — times, prices and an easy route.
keywords: Phetchaburi 2 day itinerary, Phetchaburi travel plan, Khao Wang, Cha-Am, Phetchaburi old town
h1:
Phetchaburi in 2 Days
Old Town – Khao Wang – Cha-Am
intro: Phetchaburi makes for an easy weekend trip — about 2 hours' drive from Bangkok, but you still get the whole package: an old town with beautiful temples and legendary Thai sweets, Khao Wang hill where you can see the whole city laid out below, and Cha-Am beach with fresh seafood to finish. This plan keeps the route flowing in one direction so you're never doubling back, and it works whether you're driving yourself or coming by van.

blocks.html: Phetchaburi fits a two-day trip well because the sights sit close together. Day one covers the old town and Khao Wang in the city center, then you shift south in the evening to sleep in Cha-Am. Day two you wake up to the sea breeze, eat seafood, and pick up some local treats before heading home. This rhythm means you never have to rush, and you still get time to sit in a cafe along the way.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: If you're driving, take Rama II Road south and you'll reach the city in about 2 hours. Coming by public transport, there are vans and buses from Bangkok's Southern Bus Terminal to Phetchaburi, then you can grab a motorbike taxi or rent a vehicle in town. It gets busy on long weekends, so leaving early makes the whole day easier.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Old town, temples, sweets, then up Khao Wang

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Phetchaburi Old Town → Khao Wang → Cha-Am

items.activity: Leave Bangkok, head for downtown Phetchaburi
items.note: Leave early to beat the traffic and you'll reach the city around 10:30, just in time for a late breakfast in the old town.

items.activity: Wat Mahathat Worawihan — the white five-spired prang in the city center
items.note: The town's landmark temple. Take your time with the stucco work and murals; entry is free, dress modestly, and allow about 40 minutes.

items.activity: Wat Yai Suwannaram — the teakwood sermon hall and carved doors
items.note: Just a few minutes from Wat Mahathat. This is Phetchaburi craftsmanship at its best — don't skip it if you're into woodwork and architecture.

items.activity: Lunch in the old town + Phetchaburi sweets
items.note: Try khao chae (if you're here in the hot season) or a bowl of noodles in town, then move on to mor kaeng custard, thong yip and thong yot. Phetchaburi sweets are easy to find all over town.

items.activity: Cafe time in the old town, escaping the afternoon heat
items.note: Several cafes have opened in old shophouses around the town streets over the past few years — a good spot to dodge the sun and take a few photos before heading up the hill.

items.activity: Phra Nakhon Khiri Historical Park (Khao Wang)
items.note: Take the funicular tram up and back, see the summer palace from the reign of King Rama IV, and the city views all around. Late afternoon is the sweet spot — softer sun, cooler breeze. Watch out for the monkeys on the hill.

items.activity: Come down from the hill, drive on to Cha-Am
items.note: It's about 40–45 minutes from town to Cha-Am. Check in at your beachfront stay and rest up before dinner.
Stroll along the beach, catch the sea breeze, then find a seafood spot to close out day one.

blocks.html: Khao Wang is the highlight of day one. Entry for Thais is in the tens of baht, and the tram up and down is another 50 THB or so. It opens around 08:30–16:30, so if you want to go up the hill, allow enough time to arrive before 4 pm. You can climb the stairs if you're up for it, but the tram is far more comfortable — and there are plenty of monkeys at the top, so keep your snacks and plastic bags well out of sight.

blocks.title: About the monkeys on Khao Wang
blocks.html: The monkeys here are used to people and quick to grab bags. If you're carrying a snack bag or water bottle, tuck it into your bag, don't tease them, and don't feed them. Walk calmly and you usually won't have any trouble.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Phetchaburi trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Phetchaburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.html: Cha-Am has stays across every budget, from beachfront resorts to guesthouses tucked down the side streets. If you want to wake up to the sea, pick the zone right on Cha-Am beach or quieter Puek Tian beach. On a tighter budget, choose somewhere set a little further back and walk or drive out to the beach. Weekday rates run noticeably cheaper than weekends.

items.name: Cha-Am beachfront zone
items.blurb: Walk straight to the sea, with restaurants and beach rentals all on hand. Best if you want the full beach atmosphere.

items.name: Puek Tian beach zone
items.blurb: Quieter and less crowded than Cha-Am. Good for families or anyone who actually wants to unwind.

items.name: Side streets off the beach
items.blurb: Lighter on the wallet, a few minutes' drive to the sand. Worth it on a limited budget.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Cha-Am beach, seafood, then local treats for the road

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Cha-Am Beach → Seafood → Ban Laem souvenirs → Home

items.activity: Early start for the sea breeze, a walk along Cha-Am beach
items.note: Mornings are gentle before the sun gets strong — perfect for a walk or photos. Some stretches offer horseback rides along the sand.

items.activity: Breakfast at your stay, or a seaside cafe
items.note: Cha-Am has several new seaside cafes these days. Sip a coffee with a sea view before you start the day.

items.activity: Check out, one more swim or beach time
items.note: If you want to swim, allow time to rinse off and change. Most places check out at noon.

items.activity: Fresh seafood lunch before leaving Cha-Am
items.note: Cha-Am's seafood restaurants are affordable. Steamed blue crab, grilled prawns and fried sea bass are dishes plenty of places do well.

items.activity: Stop at Ban Laem / Laem Phak Bia for seafood souvenirs
items.note: Ban Laem is the source for Phetchaburi's dried seafood and fish sauce. Pick up dried shrimp, dried squid and real fish sauce to take home.
Leaving in the late afternoon helps you dodge some of the Sunday-evening traffic on the way back. Grab some mor kaeng custard at a roadside stall before you get home.

blocks.html: Day two is all about relaxing with the sea and the food — no need to cram in activities, since day one was already a full walking day. If you've still got energy and like nature, you can swing by Laem Phak Bia for birdwatching and mangroves, or carry on toward Kaeng Krachan. But for a two-day trip, finishing with seafood and a few souvenirs is just right, without wearing yourself out.

blocks.text: Cha-Am & Ban Laem seafood — the places people actually go

blocks.html: Seafood is the standout of this trip. Cha-Am and Ban Laem sit right on the Gulf of Thailand, so the catch is fresh and the prices aren't brutal. These are the spots with steady reviews that are still open — compare them and pick the one nearest your stay.

items.name: Ban Krua Thalay Cha-Am
items.blurb: A Cha-Am seafood spot people mention often. Standouts include yum with raw salted-egg crab, fried grouper with chili and salt, and prawns in tamarind sauce. Fresh ingredients, bold full-flavored cooking.

items.name: Sirikanya Seafood
items.blurb: A long-running seafood restaurant on Cha-Am beach. Recommended: steamed squid with egg and lime, blue crab fried in curry powder, and steamed blue crab. Easy to order, good across the board.

items.name: Phon Thalay Seafood
items.blurb: Sea views and a nice atmosphere. Steamed blue crab, mantis shrimp fried with garlic, crab stir-fried with black pepper, sea bass fried with fish sauce. Good for a long, lingering meal.

items.name: View Thalay Seafood (Ban Laem)
items.blurb: A family-run place with a shady, relaxed feel and fresh ingredients daily. Friendly seafood prices — a good lunch stop before you shop for souvenirs.

items.name: Ban Thalay Seafood Laem Phak Bia
items.blurb: Seafood straight from the fishing boats to the table. Sit out and catch the natural sea breeze on Khlong Thian road. Open from early morning.

blocks.title: Ordering seafood without overpaying
blocks.html: Order steamed blue crab and grilled prawns by weight, and ask the price per kilo first. Fresh catch prices rise and fall with the season, and popular spots get long queues on long weekends — call ahead to book a table to be safe.

items: Mor kaeng (baked custard) — Phetchaburi's signature treat, fragrant and richly sweet. The famous shops line Phetkasem Road on the way in and out of town.
Thong yip, thong yot, foi thong — classic Thai golden sweets that Phetchaburi does especially well. Find them in the old town and souvenir shops.
Real palm sugar — a local sweetness from the toddy palm, used in desserts or eaten on its own.
Ban Laem dried seafood — dried shrimp, dried squid and real fish sauce, straight from the fishing source.

faq.q: Is 2 days and 1 night enough for Phetchaburi?
faq.a: It's enough for the old town–Khao Wang–Cha-Am route. Day one covers the temples and Khao Wang in town, then you head down to sleep in Cha-Am. Day two you catch the sea breeze, eat seafood and pick up souvenirs on the way back. If you want to add Kaeng Krachan or Laem Phak Bia properly, stretch it to 3 days, 2 nights.

faq.q: What are Khao Wang's hours and entry fee?
faq.a: Phra Nakhon Khiri Historical Park (Khao Wang) is open around 08:30–16:30. Entry for Thais is in the tens of baht, around 150 THB for foreigners, plus about 50 THB for the funicular tram up and down. Aim to arrive before 4 pm so you have time to walk around and catch the tram.

faq.q: Is Phetchaburi far from Bangkok, and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's about a 2-hour drive from Bangkok via Rama II. For public transport, there are vans and buses from the Southern Bus Terminal to downtown Phetchaburi and Cha-Am. If you come by bus or van, renting a vehicle or using motorbike taxis is the easy way to get around town.

faq.q: Where's good for seafood in Cha-Am?
faq.a: The spots people return to include Ban Krua Thalay, Sirikanya Seafood and Phon Thalay Seafood. Over on the Ban Laem–Laem Phak Bia side there's View Thalay Seafood and Ban Thalay Seafood. The catch is fresh and prices are reasonable — book a table ahead on weekends.

faq.q: What's the best season to visit Phetchaburi?
faq.a: You can visit year-round, but the hot season from March to May is when you'll get authentic Phetchaburi khao chae. In the rainy season the sea can get choppy with on-and-off rain, so if you're set on swimming at Cha-Am, avoid the heavy-rain days.
